keypoints.name: Motor Throttling Without Props
keypoints.description: The speaker details why motors might not throttle down on the bench without props, explaining how the PID controller tries to compensate for the lack of lift.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Addressed in a dedicated section with a specific explanation of the PID controller's behavior; appears multiple times.

the PID controller is active as soon as you lift the throttle on the quad.

keypoints.name: Props on Wrong (Orientation)
keypoints.description: The speaker describes two ways the props can be on incorrectly: props being on upside down, and props being in the wrong direction. Both cause issues like the quad being pinned or fluttering, or not lifting.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Central topic, described at length, with visual references and explanation of the leading edge.
representative_quotes: If your quad appears to be stuck to the table, it might not be your props.
A lot of people know what modes are going on and if it's active or not.  But what is the most common thing and what causes that to happen more often than not is the props being on wrong.

keypoints.name: Motor Direction (Configuration)
keypoints.description: The speaker goes over how to check and correct motor direction in Betaflight, with props off, using the motor direction wizard, and ensuring it matches the diagrams.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Substantial explanation with hands-on instruction about using Betaflight's tools to get motor direction corrected.

keypoints.name: Flight Controller Board Orientation
keypoints.description: The speaker explains how to check and correct the flight controller board orientation using the accelerometer in Betaflight's setup tab to align the virtual model's movements with the physical quad's.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Extensively covered, using Betaflight and the accelerometer as a guide. Checking and adjusting board orientation is the primary solution to a "death roll"
representative_quotes: Flight controllers do have a direction.
You have to deem the axis. And the only way to do that is with board orientation.

keypoints.name: Mechanical Failure / Flyaway
keypoints.description: The speaker discusses flyaways, usually caused by mechanical failures (frame cracks, loose assembly) or filtering problems leading to oscillations, recommending a thorough frame inspection and reverting to Betaflight defaults for maiden flights.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: A final potential cause, mechanical or tuning, discussed at length with recommendations.

And usually a flyaway is because the quad is under filtered.
